accepted.reason: Best observation-target alignment given surveillance semantics: hospitalization rate plausibly tracks infections with a short lag, and delayed_I avoids adding a potentially weakly identifiable explicit H compartment in a 31-week single-season fit. Complexity is parsimonious (non-fractional SEIRS) and consistent with current discovery patterns already favoring delayed_I with delay=2.

Reasonable near-neighbor lag sensitivity check while keeping the same parsimonious SEIRS + delayed_I mapping. A 1-week lag is still plausible for admissions in some settings/age groups and does not add identifiability burden beyond the delay choice; useful to guard against systematic phase error if the true lag is shorter than 2 weeks.

A 3-week delayed_I remains within plausible hospitalization/reporting lag ranges and keeps the same simple compartment structure, but is more likely to induce phase lag and oversmoothing for moderate-peak single-season dynamics. Acceptable only as a low-priority boundary check on lag uncertainty.

rejected.reason: Fractional memory is not clearly justified by the series summary (single season, n_train=31) and adds flexibility that can mimic delay/waning effects, increasing overfitting and identifiability risk. Given the explicit risk note about weak identifiability in short series, adding fractional dynamics on top of SEIRS+delay is more likely to create parameter tradeoffs (memory vs. delay vs. waning) than to reflect a well-supported mechanism.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify that delay is intended as an admissions/ascertainment lag (not reporting artifact) and note that with weekly aggregation, 1-week vs 2-week delays may be hard to distinguish; position this as a phase-sensitivity check rather than a mechanistic claim.

Explicitly frame delay=3 as an upper-bound sensitivity run; acknowledge higher risk of peak timing bias (late peak) and consider constraining other timing-related degrees of freedom (e.g., avoid simultaneously increasing flexibility elsewhere) to reduce confounding with the longer delay.

If kept at all, restrict its role to a single robustness probe with strong parsimony language: fix delay at 2 (as proposed) and explicitly justify why fractional memory is expected biologically/behaviorally in this setting; otherwise drop to avoid overfitting/identifiability issues in 31-week training data.
